newsitem.title: USA: L'Oreal unit buys rights to drug --NYT.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal unit buys rights to drug --NYT.

text.p: A subsidiary of L'Oreal SA has acquired the European rights to a new prostate cancer drug for as much as $68 million, the New York Times said.
The newspaper said in Monday editions that L'Oreal unit Synthelabo had acquired the rights from Praecis Pharmaceuticals Inc, a privately held biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
Under the deal L'Oreal will also finance the development of the drug for the European market and pay $10 million for a minority stake in Praecis.
Human clinical trials are currently being conducted on the treatment, which is code-named PPI-149.
The drug is shown to reduce testosterone, which is essential in the growth of prostate tissue and prostate cancer cells, to levels comparable to that achieved with castration.
